verdict.rationale: Qdrant documents snapshots as tar archives containing a collection's data and configuration, and it is Apache-2.0 open source and self-hostable on any infrastructure, so data can be taken out and run elsewhere without vendor lock-in. However, the evidence shows no export into open, tool-neutral formats: snapshot contents are Qdrant's own storage, not documented as interchangeable. Snapshots are also per collection and per node, so a full export is not a single step. Missing for 10: documented export to open formats (e.g. JSON/Parquet/CSV of vectors and payloads), a whole-account/cluster export path for cloud users, and hands-on corroboration of migrating off Qdrant.
